title: Chase the sun
text: Shoot in an hour after sunrise or before sunset. The warm light is softer and adds natural depth that the afternoon sun cannot match.

title: Use leading lines
text: Roads, railings, and rivers can pull the focus straight to your subject. Look for lines before you look for the shot.

title: Change your perspective
text: Crouch down, climb up, or get closer. Shooting from eye-level is the default, so it's rarely the most interesting angle.

title: Watch your background
text: A great subject can be ruined by mess behind it. Scan the whole frame, not just the center, before you take the picture.

title: Leave some white space
text: Empty sky, plain walls, and still water aren't wasted space. They give your subject room to breathe and stand out.

title: Steady your shot
text: Steady your camera, even small movement blurs long exposures.

title: Know the rules, then break them
text: Composition guidelines are a starting point. Some of the best shots come from ignoring them on purpose.
